text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.

- Professional classification in Finland to be restructured to conform to international standards. The new structure, to be based on job quality and skill, differs from the Nordic one based on sectoral classification.
- Central Trade Union chief Lauri Ihalainen says money allocated to so-called education insurance should be directed towards creating jobs for the long-term unemployed. @
- Member of EU parliament Paavo Vayrynen has challenged speaker of parliament Riita Ousukainen in an open letter to justify calling him a liar in her recent controversial book.
- Former EU Commissioner Jacques Delors at a seminar in Helsinki called for EMU to be more socialist and member countries' economies to be more deeply coordinated.
- Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen says Finland should reorient its thoughts and economy to the fact that the third phase of EMU is going to be fulfilled according to timetable. @
- The research department of wage earners is cautious about next year's economic growth, sees it around 3.5 percent unlike the six per cent floated by ministry of labour's Pertti Sorsa last week.
- There has been an unexpected 13 per cent growth in the electronic consumer market this year.
- Newspaper and magazine readership has fallen since the beginning of last year, says National media research institute. @
- Telephone companies fear line congestion next week due to changes in trunk numbers which customers may not be aware of.
- Central Union of wage earners, SAK, STTK and Akava to form unemployed support groups in response to ministry of labour's initiative to spend 50 million markka for unemployed support activities. @
Second Finance Minister Arja Alho supports shortening notice period of workers, saying it will create jobs for young people.
